comment: Who may satisfy the independent-review requirement recorded in D-026.
Keyed on GitHub's numeric account id, which is immutable. A login can be
renamed, and a deleted login can be re-registered by someone else; the id
cannot be transferred either way. The login is carried alongside it for
diagnostics only and is never what the verifier matches on.
This list is what makes a reviewer acceptable. Adding an entry is a
governance change requiring Friedl's approval through CODEOWNERS.
bootstrap: How Qodo came to be on this list, recorded because the circumstances were
unusual and should not be repeated silently.
Friedl approved Qodo independently, on the evidence of pull request #18: an
unaided review at head 425581b that produced fourteen anchored findings, six
of which no other reviewer reported. That approval was a governance decision
made before this entry existed. Qodo was never asked to decide whether Qodo
should be trusted.
This change was nevertheless evaluated while the blocking check still read
its reviewer roster from the pull request's own merge tree rather than from
the trusted base. Qodo therefore counted as accepted, during the very change
that accepts it, because the change says so. That is a self-authorisation
flaw in the verifier, not evidence about Qodo, and it is recorded here
rather than left for someone to discover later.
Reviewing this change, Qodo also found a second independence defect: the
verifier builds its author set from each commit's GitHub author.id alone and
ignores Co-authored-by attribution, so an accepted reviewer credited as a
co-author could still satisfy the independence requirement D-026 states. The
finding is valid and was reproduced. It is deliberately not fixed here,
because this entry is a governance record rather than a verifier change.
Both defects must be closed in the hardening change that follows this merge
immediately, in which the verifier, this roster and the exception register
are all loaded from the GitHub-attested base revision, and independence
detection recognises commit co-authors.
Friedl authorised this bootstrap once, for this entry only. It is not a
precedent: no future reviewer may be added by a change that relies on its
own contents to be trusted.
